summary: Sketch dimensions on the canvas are now selected before they are edited. Hovering a dimension's value, line or arrows highlights the points, lines, arcs and circles it measures; hovering a row in the relations or constraint issues list highlights the same geometry, including the origin or axis that a coordinate is measured from. A click selects one dimension and replaces the geometry selection, Shift toggles, Escape clears, and the status line names the selection. Double-click or Enter opens the existing editor; Space selects. Opening the editor, also from Edit value…, keeps the dimension selected and leaves the geometry unselected, so Delete removes the dimension, never the geometry it measures, while the editor is open and after Apply or Cancel. The editor selects only the dimension it edits. In the relations list, also when it opens from a point's or curve's Constraints and dimensions or Dimension menu, opening a dimension's row makes that dimension the selection, so switching rows moves the selection, and opening another relation's row returns the selection to the geometry the list belongs to. The editor belongs to its part, sketch and dimension: it closes when geometry, the sketch origin or an axis, a profile or another dimension takes the selection, or when another part opens under the same IDs, and selecting a dimension clears the origin and axes. Cancel closes the editor for good: a later Escape, or an edit that remounts the relations list, never reopens or focuses it, and a row closed in the list stays closed. Delete or Backspace removes the selected dimensions in one undo step through the same prepared edit as the relations list, and a refused removal keeps them with its message. Keyboard focus never changes the selection, so Tab moves through dimensions, points and edges without closing an editor: Delete or Backspace on a focused dimension label or profile chip, and Delete on a focused point or edge, remove the current selection, what is drawn selected, and the focused item only while nothing is selected; Backspace removes only dimensions, and with the origin, an axis or a legacy profile selected a focused label removes nothing. Point to line distances, also those measured from an arc or circle center, select, edit, highlight their point and line, convert with Make reference and Make driving and delete like the other dimensions. A right-click menu offers Edit value…, Make reference or Make driving, and Delete; commands that do not apply stay visible, disabled, with the reason. Dimensions draw thinner: no label box, 1 px lines, slimmer arrows, quieter extension lines and haloed monospace values in theme colours, with reference values in parentheses and a dimmer colour. A selection, keyboard focus and an open menu belong to the dimension they were made on: a new value, Make reference and Make driving keep it selected, and so does a Trim or Extend that moves an end of a referenced line; a dimension that undo, redo or an agent edit removes, or replaces with another measurement under the same ID, comes back unselected and without focus, a closing menu or editor does not return focus to the replacement, and a menu closes without running a command when the sketch changes or the edit is cancelled. The size chips on older and plugin profiles draw as plain haloed values like the canvas dimensions, through a new shared annotation button appearance, and follow the same rules: a click selects and highlights the leader, double-click or Enter edits and selects only the chip it edits, opening another part closes a chip editor and clears the chip selection, Delete removes a driving dimension, and the menu offers Edit value…, a disabled Make reference with its reason, and Delete. Accessible names change: canvas dimensions read Dimension or Reference dimension, the quantity and value, then press Enter to edit, instead of Configure or Inspect reference; profile chips read Dimension, the quantity and value, then press Enter to edit, instead of Edit and the quantity.
warning: Potentially breaking for automation and people that click a dimension expecting its editor: a click now only selects, and a double-click or Enter opens the editor. Automation that finds a canvas dimension by its accessible name must use the new names, for example Dimension distance 15 mm, press Enter to edit instead of Configure distance 15 mm, and Reference dimension diameter 6 mm, press Enter to edit instead of Inspect reference diameter 6 mm. Profile size chips change from Edit Width to Dimension width 30 mm, press Enter to edit. Delete with a dimension selected removes the dimension, not geometry. Delete on a focused point, edge, dimension label or profile chip now removes the current selection when something else is selected, where it used to remove the focused item, and Backspace on a focused dimension label with geometry selected removes nothing; automation that focused an item to delete it must select it first. While the editor of a canvas dimension is open, cad_get_viewport.selectedSketchGeometrySet is empty: opening the editor by double-click, Enter or Edit value… keeps the dimension selected instead of selecting the geometry it measures, so automation that read the edited geometry from the viewport selection must read the relation from the document instead. The same applies when a dimension's row is opened in the relations list, including a list opened from a geometry's Constraints and dimensions or Dimension menu: that dimension becomes the selection and selectedSketchGeometrySet empties, and opening a relation that is not a dimension restores the geometry. Opening an editor on one of several selected dimensions or chips selects that one alone, and an open dimension editor closes when a legacy profile, the sketch origin or an axis is selected or another part opens. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD documents or controller output.

checklist.schema: No CAD schema change: removals use the existing remove-sketch-relation and remove-sketch-dimension edits, and conversions use set-sketch-relation with the existing reference-dimension, distance, point-line-distance and radial-size kinds. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol change; the Rust solver and committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. Hover runs no solver or analysis call and renders only the highlight overlay; moving the pointer across a dimension label, line or arrow, or across relation and issue rows, does not render the sketch canvas. Canvas and chip menus close, and their commands are dropped, when the part, version, build or sketch changed, the edit was cancelled, or the dimension was replaced after the menu opened. Selections keep the dimension identity they were made on, so a reused relation or constraint ID never inherits one. Keyboard focus is bound to the same identity: a replacement under the same ID mounts a new label or chip, so neither focus nor a closing menu or editor returns to it, and Delete, Backspace and menu commands check the identity before they run. A line-length reference is identified by its line, so a Trim or Extend that rewrites an endpoint keeps it selected. A canvas dimension editor records the part identity, sketch and dimension it belongs to, and closes in the same render once the selection is anything but that dimension alone or the part identity changes; the relations panel reports the row it edits, so the selection follows a row switch, and a closed row is recorded in the command, so a remounted panel keeps it closed. Cancel drops the open relations command, so neither a later Escape nor a remount focuses a cancelled editor, and another part or sketch clears the selection during render, before a relations row can mount or take focus in it. Keyboard focus never moves the selection: Delete and Backspace on a focused label, chip, point or edge act on the selection, which menus select on opening. Profile chip editors close when the part identity changes. WebMCP tools and their arguments are unchanged, and dimension selection is not part of the agent viewport state. One viewport value changes: cad_get_viewport.selectedSketchGeometrySet is empty while a canvas dimension editor is open, including one opened from the relations list, where it used to hold the measured geometry; docs/site/agents.md says so.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. Canvas dimensions and profile chips gain selection, hover highlight, Delete and a context menu; double-click or Enter opens the editor that a click opened before. Opening that editor, from the canvas, a relations list row or a geometry menu, no longer selects the measured geometry: the editor works on it while the dimension alone is selected. Point to line distances gain Make reference and Make driving from the canvas menu, using the existing point-line-distance reference measurement and keeping the side the point is on. The shared Button gains an annotation variant and theme.css gains the --annotation-halo token; existing variants are unchanged.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved documents open unchanged and older releases open documents edited with this one.
checklist.verification: Full Vitest passed after merging main at 0.0.778: 555 files, 6340 tests. cadSketchDimensionSelection unit tests cover selection, the dimension identity rules (value edits, Make reference and Make driving keep a pick; a reused ID that measures something else drops it; a line reference keeps its pick when Trim or Extend rewrites an endpoint and through a later Make driving), refreshed picks, mount keys that change only on replacement, reconciliation, status text, highlight targets and the hover store; CadSketchGraphDimensions, CadSketchCanvasRender, CadSketchDimensionControls, CadGearInteraction and CadWorkbench tests cover click selection, Shift toggles, Space, Escape, Enter and double-click editing, hover highlights from labels and relation rows, one-step Delete, refused removal messages, the context menu with disabled reasons, menus that close on a replaced dimension, a part change or Cancel, selections that never pass to a reused ID, that pointer moves across labels, dimension lines, arrows, relation rows and issue rows render only the overlay, that Enter, double-click and Edit value… keep the dimension selected with no geometry selected so Delete removes only the dimension before and after Apply and Cancel, that focus, a closing menu or editor, and a right-press never pass to a replacement label or chip, that a relations row switch, a geometry menu's Constraints and dimensions or Dimension, and a non-dimension row move the selection with the edited row, that an editor opened on one of several selected dimensions or chips selects it alone, and that a legacy profile selection or another part under the same IDs closes a canvas or chip dimension editor. Round 4 tests check that Delete and Backspace on a focused label, chip, point or edge remove the selection and the focused item only while nothing is selected, that Escape after Cancel never focuses or reopens a cancelled editor, for an existing and a new dimension, that a closed row stays closed when an edit remounts the relations list, and that a non-dimension row never takes focus in another part. After the merge, a point to line distance made by the circle double-pick selects, edits on its center and line, highlights both, converts with Make reference and Make driving and deletes, and a datum selection and a dimension selection replace each other, an axis closes an open editor and a focused label deletes nothing past a selected axis. Each round 2, 3 and 4 test, and each merge test, fails with its fix reverted; the round 4 mutations were rerun after the merge. tsc -b, npm run build, npm run lint, npm run ui:check, npm run docs:check and node scripts/check-release.mjs origin/main pass. Chromium specs with --workers=2 pass: cad-sketch-dimension-selection 1/1, cad-sketch-constraints 27/27, cad-sketch-reference-dimensions 1/1, cad-sketch-selectable-axes 1/1 and cad-workflow 32/32; the cad-sketch-constraints point editing step now selects Point 2 with Space before Delete, because a refused nudge selects Point 1 and Delete acts on the selection. No controller or machine verification applies because output is unchanged.

publicNotes.summary: Sketch dimensions select on click and edit on double-click.
changes: Hover a dimension, or a row in the relations list, to highlight the geometry it measures, including the origin or axis for a coordinate.
Click a dimension to select it, Shift-click to add or remove one and Escape to clear. Double-click or press Enter to edit it.
Opening a dimension's editor keeps the dimension selected, so Delete removes the dimension and never the geometry it measures.

Opening a dimension in the relations list, also from a point's or curve's menu, selects that dimension alone; switching rows moves the selection, and the editor closes when you select something else or open another part.
Keyboard focus never changes the selection: Delete on a focused dimension, point or edge removes what is selected, and the focused item only when nothing is.
Delete or Backspace removes the selected dimensions in one undo step. Right-click a dimension for Edit value…, Make reference or Make driving, and Delete; unavailable commands explain why.
Dimensions draw with thin lines and plain values; reference values show in parentheses in a dimmer colour.
The size chips on older and plugin profiles draw as plain values like the canvas dimensions and follow the same click, double-click, Delete and right-click rules.

A selection, keyboard focus or open menu stays with its dimension: a dimension replaced by an edit or brought back by undo starts unselected and without focus, a menu closes when the sketch changes, and a reference to a line's length stays selected through Trim and Extend.
Point to line distances, also from an arc or circle center, select, edit, convert and delete like the other dimensions, and selecting the origin or an axis replaces a dimension selection.
publicNotes.compatibility: Sketches keep using existing relation and dimension kinds, so earlier releases open them. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: Double-click a dimension, or press Enter on it, where a single click used to open its editor, and select a dimension, point or edge before deleting it from the keyboard. Automation that finds dimensions by accessible name should use the new names, such as Dimension distance 15 mm, press Enter to edit. While a dimension editor is open, including one opened from the relations list, the agent viewport now reports no selected geometry.
